Subject: Annual planning: targets + what-if triage / QBR roadtest

Team —

We need to start the FY27 planning thread that will feed the QBR decks and the exec target conversation in May. I attached an initial scenario matrix (FY27_scenario_matrix_v1.xlsx) with three high-level revenue bands and associated cost levers. Goal for this thread: agree on a small set (2–3) of planning scenarios, an aggressive and a stress-tested baseline, and a realistic timeline to bake these into QBR materials.

Immediate asks:
- Can each of you flag missing assumptions in the spreadsheet by Monday EOD? I circled where I think capacity and price sensitivity matter most.
- Laura: can you propose an initial targets band (stretch / base / safety) for hosting & revenue by Apr 22?
- Tessa: propose a draft timeline for reviews and QBR artifacts (slides + appendix) that works with your org cadence.
- Vivek: we need region-level impacts (APAC latency/region capacity) included — can you confirm if we should model an APAC downside?

I'll run a short roadtest: invite to a 45m sync next Wed 4/21 to walk the scenarios and gate decisions. If we converge on a baseline, we should also lock the evaluation prompts for Redwood Optimize that will measure quality regressions against cost changes.

Thanks — short thread, direct asks.

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP Product, Redwood Inference

Markus — thanks for the clear asks. Quick notes after a first pass on the spreadsheet:

- Assumptions: the churn line looks optimistic versus last cycle; recommend modeling +1.5% churn in the stress scenario (we saw a similar delta in FY25).
- Targets band (first pass):
  - Stretch: ARR $195M, Hosting margin target 42%
  - Base: ARR $170M, Hosting margin 38%
  - Safety: ARR $150M, Hosting margin 33%

- I'll add these to a tab in the workbook and flag the underlying drivers (sales velocity, conversion, retention).
- On QBR artifacts: let's include a short appendix with the scenario assumptions and a one-slide sensitivity chart (ARR vs. token price / batch efficiency).

I'll upload a version with notes by EOD Monday. If it helps, I can own the sensitivity slide and the appendix.

-Laura

Markus / team —

APAC note: we should absolutely model an APAC downside for the stress scenario. Two quick inputs:
- Capacity: GCP quotas in APAC could reduce burst throughput by ~20% in Q4 in the constrained case. That needs to show up in cost per call unless we assume cross-region failover.
- Pricing sensitivity: if we need to push traffic to US/EU for capacity, add a 3–5% hosting cost premium in the stress model.

I'll load a region tab into the spreadsheet with the above numbers and a short note on assumptions. Also linking PL-4823 which captures the capacity work.

-Vivek
